newsitem.title: USA: Atlanta hit with sewer hook-up moratorium.
newsitem.headline: Atlanta hit with sewer hook-up moratorium.

text.p: Georgia regulators have imposed a three-month moratorium on Atlanta construction projects that require new sewer hook-ups because the city failed to meet water pollution controls, a spokesman for Mayor Bill Campbell said Tuesday.

Spokesman Nick Gold said the mayor received a letter from the Georgia Environmental Protection Division on Monday notifying him that water the city discharged into the Chattahoochee River in February exceeded phosphorous limits.
The department imposed a three month moratorium and fined the city $750,000.
The Atlanta City Council was scheduled to vote later Tuesday on a 14 percent sewer rate increase to help pay for sewer system upgrades designed to end the pollution.
Campbell has proposed that the city issue $180 million of revenue bonds to make the upgrades, paying debt service with the new fees and with savings achieved by privatizing water-sewer operations.

Gold said that while the council must approve the rate increase, the mayor can proceed with the privatization plan without council approval. He said Campbell would hire a consultant "in the next few weeks" to draft a request for proposals from firms seeking to operate the water-sewer system, which would remain under city ownership.

The Atlanta Journal-Constitution identified three privately owned firms Tuesday as primary contenders -- Professional Services Group, JMM Operations Services Inc and Operations Management International.
Gold said he could not confirm that they were top contenders but said Campbell "has been in conversation with three of the world's top firms" in drafting the privatization proposal.
